newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sees $1.5 billion extra oil revenue.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees $1.5 billion extra oil revenue.

text.p: Iran expects revenue from oil exports to exceed budget forecasts by $1.5 billion if prices continue to improve for the rest of the year, an official was quoted as saying on Saturday.

"Iranian oil revenues for the current fiscal year would go up by $1.5 billion compared to the budget forecasts if prices continue to rise," Qorbanali Dorri-Najafabadi, head of the Iran's planning and budget commission told the Iranian news agency IRNA.
The agency also quoted a report carried on Saturday by Iranian television saying oil revenue in the five months from March to August 1996 was $600 million over budget forecasts.
"While current year budget was based on the price of $15.5, Iranian oil was sold at the average price of $17.8 per barrel," the report said.
Najafabadi said "the new situation in the oil markets has stemmed from the developments in northern Iraq and U.S. provocations in the region."
Oil prices soared to their highest levels since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis following renewed tension in the region.

An incursion in August by Baghdad's troops to assist a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq prompted 44 U.S. cruise missile strikes on targets in southern Iraq and a major U.S. military buildup in the Gulf to guard against further military action by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
Iranian officials said earlier they expected hard currency revenue, which comes mainly from crude oil exports, to exceed budget forecasts by $2 billion.
The budget for the current Iranian year which started on March 20, envisaged petroleum earnings of $15.99 billion, based on exports of 2.6 million barrels per day.

Iran, an OPEC member and the world's third largest oil exporter, has said its revenue from crude oil exports in the previous fiscal year which ended on March 19, 1996 was $1.6 billion above that set in the budget.
The report said oil revenues in the five months from March were $7.2 billion.
